label: Счастливый / Несчастный
description: Счастливый vs несчастный: happy/unhappy contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Счастливый' takes the masculine ending to match 'день'. The everyday remark anchors the form in a common moment.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Несчастная' takes the feminine ending to match 'судьба'. The sentence places the form in a reflective context.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Счастливое' takes the neuter ending to match 'детство'. The warm memory makes the neuter form concrete.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Счастливые' takes the plural ending to match 'дети'. The lively image fixes the plural form in mind.
Strategic focus: Direct masculine contrast. 'Счастливый' is nominative for 'человек' while 'несчастному' is dative for the recipient 'другу'. One sentence pairs happy against unhappy.
Strategic focus: Short-form masculine predicate. The short form 'счастлив' states a present feeling of the subject and is very common in speech. Short forms suit a current emotional state.
Strategic focus: Short-form feminine predicate. 'Счастлива' is the feminine short form after past-tense 'была'. The celebration roots the form in an everyday occasion.

missions.phrase: После аварии он чувствовал себя несчастным.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine instrumental in the predicate. After 'чувствовал себя', 'несчастным' takes the instrumental ending describing the subject. This shows the reflexive-plus-instrumental pattern.

Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'несчастными' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'они'. The sentence extends the быть-plus-instrumental pattern into the plural.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Счастливее' is the comparative of 'счастливый' and stays the same for any gender. The warm statement shows the comparative in everyday use.
